entry.title: UFC Paris: Michael 'Venom' Page wins in underwhelming UFC farewell - BBC
entry.body: Fans boo as MVP wins in underwhelming UFC farewell - Published Michael 'Venom' Page's last fight on his UFC contract ended in an underwhelming win against Nursulton Ruziboev amid booing fans in Paris. London's Page, who is nicknamed 'MVP', landed a handful of eye-catching strikes during the contest but could not deliver the knockout that the fans craved as he won by unanimous decision. The 39-year-old's victory means all five of his wins in the UFC since joining in 2024 have come via decision. Page joined the UFC with a reputation as an innovative striker with a resume of highlight-reel knockouts, but admitted pre-fight he has underperformed since joining the organisation. Page said the fight with Uzbekistan's Ruziboev was "important to re-establish myself with the UFC", but he did not get the finish he wanted. Page, who arrived in the UFC over two years ago with 13 knockouts to his name, received a raucous ovation from the French crowd as he entered the octagon. Ruziboev controlled the majority of the first round on the ground before Page started to open up midway through the fight. He landed a kick to Ruziboev's knee which wobbled the 32-year-old, before smiling and showboating as he delivered a number of feints. Page delivered an overhead right and an elbow, but the explosive moments were few and far between as the crowd grew frustrated at a lack of action. Throughout the bout, Page landed only 12 significant strikes to Ruziboev's eight. Page has shown throughout his UFC career he is a master of movement and evasion, without having the finishing instinct that the most successful fighters possess. The fight against Ruziboev followed the same pattern, and although Page was awarded victory by the judges, his arm was raised after jeers from the crowd. With Page now a free agent, potential options for him if he does not re-sign with the UFC include joining the PFL or turning to boxing. In the main event, French-Moroccan Salahdine Parnasse earned a stunning first-round TKO win over Dan Hooker. Parnasse was making his UFC debut and delivered in front of a home crowd, landing a punishing kick to the body before dropping New Zealand's Hooker with a left hook. The 28-year-old followed with a flurry of punches as Hooker, ranked 12 in the lightweight division, shelled up on the floor, forcing the referee to wave off the contest. There was also victory for fellow Briton Kurtis Campbell, who submitted American Trevor Peek in the third round of their featherweight bout via a rear-naked choke. It was a return to winning ways for the 24-year-old Liverpudlian, who lost on his UFC debut to Danny Silva in March. Campbell's win extends his professional record to nine wins and one defeat. "I know my debut didn't go the way I wanted it to but I'm here to show I'm the real deal and the future is bright," said Campbell. Earlier on the card, London's Nathaniel Wood lost by unanimous decision to Moldova's Pavel Andrusca, bringing his four-fight win streak to an end. Andrusca, who was a late replacement after Wood's original opponent Mairon Santos withdrew 10 days prior to the fight, extended the unbeaten start to his career to nine. At UFC 322 on 3 October in Salt Lake City, it was announced Brazil's Natalia Silva will fight for the vacant flyweight title against China's Wang Cong. Former title holder Valentina Shevchenko has vacated the belt and is set to miss over a year with injury, according to the UFC. entry.title: Tears, blood & triumph - Taylor's iconic career in pictures
entry.body: Making her amateur debut in 2001, Taylor won every medal and title she could have and more importantly had a lasting effect on women's boxing and women as athletes. BBC Sport takes a look back on some of the best pictures from her iconic career. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Taylor helped legalise women boxing in Ireland, competing in the first sanctioned female fight in 2001 aged 15 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Taylor won five world championships as an amateur including in 2012 when she also won Olympic gold in London Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Her father Peter, who had been her long-time coach, was there to celebrate with her Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Taylor is one of 15 Irish athletes to win gold at an Olympics in any sport and was the only Irish gold medallist in 2012 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, She returned in 2016 but suffered a shock exit in the quarter-finals Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Taylor quickly moved on, convincing Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn to sign her as a professional. Taylor was the first female fighter Hearn signed Image source, Getty Images Image caption, She made a winning debut at Wembley Arena in November 2016, which was packed with Irish fans Image source, Getty Images Image caption, She took just 11 months to claim her first world title - the WBA lightweight belt Image source, Getty Images Image caption, In her bid to become Ireland's first four-belt world champion at Madison Square Garden in 2019, she was almost beaten by Delfine Persoon Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The wounds of war were obvious on Taylor's face after the battle with Persoon Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Taylor returned to MSG in 2022, this time to face Amanda Serrano. Years of talks finally bore fruit as the rivals finally stepped in the ring together at a sold-out MSG. entry.title: Bad Bunny ‘Super Bowl Halftime Show,’ ‘Muppets’ and ‘Traitors’ Win Night 1 Creative Arts Emmy Awards
entry.body: Bad Bunny’s “Super Bowl Halftime Show” and “The Traitors” dominated night one of the Creative Arts Emmys with seven and six wins, respectively. Comedian Wanda Sykes provided opening remarks. “Television isn’t made by a handful of people. It’s made by thousands of talented people solving impossible problems together to create something great,” she said. “So, the more excellence there is to recognize, the more time we should spend celebrating it.” The first Emmy of the evening went to late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel, who won for game show host (“Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?”). Kimmel, who won last year, thanked the seat fillers. He joked, “Mostly I really want to thank whoever decided to put our category first because we won last year, and it was nothing but seat fillers. So, thank you very much, and thanks to the seat fillers for sticking it out.” “The Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny” picked up seven Emmys, including outstanding choreography for variety or reality programming (Charm La’Donna, Karina Ortiz), outstanding production design for a variety special Bruce Rodgers), outstanding music direction (Miguel Gandelman) and outstanding variety special (live). Gandelman talked about the challenge of putting the show together. He said, “The hardest part for me was catching Benito on tour. I had to record the band, so I had to go to Colombia. I had to go to Chile.” He went on to say, “Production in L.A. had started already, so making sure that I was always on time with everything that was needed for me.” Mariska Hargitay took home two Emmys for outstanding documentary or nonfiction special and outstanding directing for “My Mom Jayne: A Film By Mariska Hargitay.” During her speech, an emotional Hargitay honored feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who died earlier this week. Hargitay said, “My hero and friend Gloria Steinem recently said, ‘Please tell your own story. The most important thing that we can do for each other is to know each other through stories.’” A tearful Hargitay said, “I got to know my mother through telling the story, and it is a gift that is indescribable.” Backstage, Hargitay talked further about Steinem and what her win meant to women. She said, “Don’t let anyone else define you. Dreaming, as Gloria said, is part of planning.” Hargitay said, “I’m at a place in my life where I just say yes. I said yes to Broadway, and I said yes to hosting the Emmys.” She went on to say, “When they called me, I thought it was a joke, and then I went, ‘Why not?” So, it’s a year of firsts and a year of saying yes and a year of not limiting myself or not being governed by fear.” She concluded by saying, “What if it all works out? That’s the process of art.” Sabrina Carpenter is now halfway to EGOT winning an Emmy in the outstanding variety special (pre-recorded) for “The Muppet Show.” Carpenter is created as an executive producer and performer for the series. Seth Rogen also took home his fifth Emmy award for his work as an executive producer. Tyler Strickland, who won the Emmy for outstanding music composition for a documentary/nonfiction or reality for “John Candy: I Like Me,” spoke backstage about his approach to scoring the film. Strickland said he recorded the entire score using a string orchestra. “For John specifically, with his theme, I gave him a French horn, which I think really spoke to valor and strength, but also was a singular instrument that I could write sad melodies on and try to give him a little bit of a synthesis.” Talking about his biggest challenge, he said, “We were making a film about somebody who’s so iconic and known for all these amazing roles, but that we weren’t making a comedic film. We were making a beautiful film about a father and a husband and a man who was struggling with anxiety.” Netflix’s “Love on a Spectrum” took home three Emmys. During his acceptance speech, casting director Sean Bowman, who won for outstanding casting for a reality program, said working on the show “is an absolute dream.” Bowman said, “I want to thank our casting team, Chelsea (Darnell, casting producer), and the cast who trusted us with their stories and the thousands of people who have written in.” Bowman went on to say, “I just love talking on Zoom and hearing their stories of why they want to find love. If you want to find love, you can find love.” Popular on Variety The previously announced juried awards were also handed out this evening. Adult Swim’s “Genndy Tartakovsky’s Primal” took home two Emmys for outstanding individual achievement in animation. Peacock’s “The Traitors” and Fox’s “The Masked Singer” were honored in the outstanding costumes for variety, nonfiction or reality programming categories. The Creative Arts Emmys are being handed out at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, and an edited presentation of the 2026 ceremonies will broadcast on Sept. 12, at 8:00 PM ET/PT on FXX. entry.title: ‘The Debut’ Review: Julianne Moore Is Astonishing in Jesse Eisenberg’s Funny and Dizzying Community-Theater Comedy
entry.body: It’s rare these days to find comedy and humanity on the same plate — and even more rare to see comedy nuzzling up to mystery. (I don’t mean mystery as in crime-solving; I mean the mystery of existence.) But Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut,” a small-town-theater comedy driven by big ideas, is a funny and dizzying mind-bender. It’s like “Waiting for Guffman” made by the Coen brothers at their most rivetingly unhinged. “The Debut” won’t be for everyone, but if you get onto its wavelength (which I did immediately), it sucks you into its “Twilight Zone of Sub-Broadway” vortex, even as the tone remains light and ticklish and surprising. Eisenberg, as he proved two years ago in the brilliant “A Real Pain,” is a grounded filmmaker (he loves reality). But here he’s working on a high wire of matter-of-fact satire that edges, just barely, into the surreal. At heart, the film is a twisted love letter to the glory of community theater. What holds it together is the suppleness of Eisenberg’s voice as a writer-director (the wit that singes, the story that never stops poking around corners), and the utterly astonishing performance of Julianne Moore, who plays a crumpled wallflower in dire need of blooming. Popular on Variety Moore’s Mona Friedman is a New Jersey homemaker who has become a Stepford zombie, because no one seems to need her anymore. Her twins, Matty (Joan Diamand) and Maya (Becca Suskauer), are nearly adults, and though they’re still living at home they’ve already checked out. Her husband, Howard (Patrick Fabian), is a handsome stiff-necked jerk who treats Mona like an accessory. And she’s such a fearful, passive people pleaser that none of this is in any danger of changing. Moore, with red eyes and translucent skin, gives off the aura of a damaged doll. In the opening scene, set in the Brook Theater, she tries out for a small role in the annual local production of “Nosy Neighbors,” and her audition is so weak that we don’t see how she could possibly get the part. It goes instead to Serena Cherry (Bernadette Peters), a Broadway wannabe who lands any role she wants. (There’s a poster of her in the lobby as the lead in a production of “Evita.”) But then, late one night, Mona gets a call from the musical’s director, Jerry (Paul Giamatti). Serena has bowed out; he’s got no one else to do the part. (It helps that she ripped off all the phone-number tags on a local flyer for the audition.) Mona comes into rehearsal the next morning (the cast has been at it for several weeks), and what we instantly see is that “Nosy Neighbors,” an upbeat musical about the residents of a downscale apartment building, is a corny but oddly sturdy piece of third-rate hokum – it’s like “Rent” redone by Corky St. (The songs, which Eisenberg composed, sound like Jonathan Larson-by-numbers.) Mona is playing Miss Danielle, the building super, a tough nut who wears a tool belt and has the signature line, “Rent’s due!” Not exactly an acting challenge. The other cast members are warm and welcoming, but Mona, who has no theatrical experience (beyond singing in her church choir until she was 13), is awful beyond words. She delivers that line as if she was whispering it in a library. She’s a doormat in life and a washout of an actress, even for community theater. So Jerry, realizing that he’s got a potential disaster on his hands, decides that his only recourse is to give Mona a tough-love private acting lesson. In a remarkable scene, he makes her ask for the rent check he’s holding in his hand — and more than that, he keeps asking her why she wants it, breaking down her defenses. It’s like a Sanford Meisner exercise turned torture session, and Mona finally busts through with a monologue that spills out of her guts, about how she wants that rent money because if she doesn’t get it she’ll be in an alley eating plague-ridden rats. She burns through her own lack of purpose and identity and, at that moment, becomes an actress. What Jerry doesn’t realize is that he’s created a monster. “The Debut” is at once an affectionate homage to the wide-eyed passion of community theater; a deftly original thriller; a parable of self-esteem; a teasing mockery of the mechanisms of self-esteem; and a one-woman psychodrama in which Mona discovers who she is by leaving her old reality behind. There’s a hilarious scene in which Jerry, as part of Mona’s Method training, takes her out to a random apartment building, and she talks her way into someone’s home by impersonating the super and demanding to fix the toilet. The thing is, the Method training works. Mona lets herself go and becomes a confident actress. Yet if that’s all there was to it, “The Debut” would just be a tidy feel-good fable. Eisenberg is too talented and ambitious to make that kind of movie. He wants instead to make our heads spin by taking us down a rabbit hole. It’s when Mona, fed up with her husband, moves out of her home and into a fleabag hotel, where the faucets drip and the dingy electric lights are buzzy and there are strange sounds coming through the walls, that the film begins to turn into a slightly dreamy hellscape. But Moore keeps us on her side. Her Mona is avid to find a new way to be, even if that means putting on a janitor suit and, after shorting out the hotel’s electricity (and burning off her eyebrows), getting a new look that makes her resemble Camille Paglia crossed with Joan Jett as styled by David Lynch. The joke, and it’s a juicy one, is that she has now gone full Method, and insists that everything her character in the musical says must be entirely reality-based. It wouldn’t work if Mona’s fearless new acting ethos weren’t so goddamn funny. And it wouldn’t work if Paul Giamatti, who’s kind of playing the audience’s surrogate, didn’t invest Jerry, the disgruntled theater romantic, with a hope and rage and bone-deep melancholy that keeps the film from flying off into the ether. The actors playing the song-and-dance cast members of “Nosy Neighbors” (they include Eisenberg) perform with sublimely subtle cluelessness. But it’s the audacity of Julianne Moore — now clenched, now grinning, now timid, now acting — that brings “The Debut” to its gratifying conclusion, as Mona, through the theater, discovers an extraordinary new role: herself.
entry.summary: What holds it together is the suppleness of Eisenberg’s voice as a writer-director (the wit that singes, the story that never stops poking around corners), and the utterly astonishing performance of Julianne Moore, who plays a crumpled-up wallflower in dire need of blooming. Oh, does she bloom.

entry.title: Danny Boyle Confirms Use Of AI In New Movie ‘Ink’ - Deadline
entry.body: Danny Boyle has confirmed the use of AI in new movie Ink about the launch of The Sun newspaper. Speaking to Vanity Fair, Boyle said he had used around 30 seconds of generative AI in the making of his new movie, which opened the Venice Film Festival this week before going on to play Telluride. “There’s about 30 seconds of it in our movie where we animate a couple of old photographs,” the Oscar winner said in a video interview from the Colorado festival. “Oh, and there’s some mice,” he added. “It’s very good for animals, and we had some mice that run around The Sun newsroom.” Some viewers of the movie took to social media this week to ponder whether AI had been used to reanimate old images of the Kray brothers and former UK Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher. Per Boyle’s video from Telluride, the answer to that would seem to be yes. Watch on Deadline Vanity Fair earlier asked Boyle what he thinks about the use of AI in film, to which he responded: “It doesn’t really matter what I think about AI. It matters what 20-year-olds think about it. My opinion of it is that it’s a very useful tool in many ways, provided you use it respectfully and provided you pay actors if you’re going to replace them with some kind of AI embodiment.” Earlier this week, speaking at the Venice press conference for Ink, Boyle had voiced concerns about the impact of AI on certain sectors, including journalism. “The danger with the tech giants and their AI is that they will be able to replace journalism. They’ll be able to have an AI journalist who’s much more efficient, cheaper, etcetera, ecetera, and will that AI journalist speak truth to the power that created it?” Ink, starring Jack O’Connell, Guy Pearce and Claire Foy, charts the rise of the UK’s notorious tabloid newspaper The Sun in the 1970s under the editorship of Larry Lamb, after he was poached from the Daily Mirror in 1969 by then budding media mogul Rupert Murdoch. The Studiocanal and Netflix film, which launches in December in cinemas and on Netflix in January, received largely positive notices out of Venice and currently counts an 85% fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

entry.title: Natalie Portman Welcomes Third Child, First With Partner Tanguy Destable - The Hollywood Reporter
entry.body: Natalie Portman is now a mom of three. Portman, 45, welcomed her third baby, her first with partner Tanguy Destable, in Paris last month, according to People. The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Portman’s reps for comment but did not hear back. The Oscar winner announced in April that she was pregnant with her third child in an interview with Harper’s Bazaar, saying she felt “very grateful,” and that it was “such a privilege and a miracle” to be expecting a baby with Destable, a French music producer. “Tanguy and I are very excited,” she said at the time. “I grew up hearing about how hard it is to get pregnant. I have so many people I love who’ve had such a hard time with it that I want to be respectful around that as well,” the Black Swan star continued. “It’s such a beautiful, joyous thing, and it’s also not an easy thing. And so I know how lucky it is. I’m very aware, and I’m very grateful. I have deep appreciation.” Portman shares two children with her ex-husband, choreographer Benjamin Millepied. People previously reported that Portman and Destable’s romance was confirmed in March 2025. In her Harper’s Bazaar interview, Portman also reflected on the perspective she has gained with age and the gratitude she felt during her third pregnancy. “There is a gratitude that when you’re young, you don’t necessarily grasp,” she said. “There’s a calm and knowing myself: who I want to spend time with, what kind of energy I want around me that makes the experience so beautiful every day. And knowing it’s probably the last time, I cherish every moment.”

entry.title: Star Trek's Gene Roddenberry Tried To Kill A Major TNG Storyline Because Of One Character - TVLine
entry.body: Star Trek's Gene Roddenberry Tried To Kill A Major TNG Storyline Because Of One Character As the creator of "Star Trek," Gene Roddenberry was innately tapped into the plotlines that made up the greater universe of the franchise — but sometimes, he didn't exactly see the vision, like when he tried to kill a major storyline on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" over one character. Somehow, Roddenberry didn't see Worf, key Klingon Starfleet officer and Federation ambassador to Qo'noS, as a major character on TNG, so he — and nearly he alone — was against centering the show's Season 4 finale around the start of a Klingon civil war. "In Gene's mind, Worf was a character that he put on the bridge just to put into the background so that you could comment on the fact that the Klingons and the Federation were at peace now," executive producer Rick Berman told the episode's writer, Ronald D. Moore, during development, according to the book "The Fifty-Year Mission: The Next 25 Years," by Mark A. The creatives surrounding Roddenberry were not on his side. "I know we all see it differently," Berman added of Michael Dorn's character. Gene doesn't want to do a whole cliffhanger about him." Worf and the Klingon civil war changed Star Trek forever At the time, leaving the "Star Trek: The Next Generation" Season 4 finale on a cliffhanger in which Worf fled the Enterprise to fight in a Klingon civil war seemed like a well-rounded arc for a dedicated supporting character — one that the show's writers seemingly thought deserved creator Gene Roddenberry's blessing. How strongly Roddenberry felt about keeping Worf out of the Season 4 finale spotlight is unclear, because ultimately, he didn't get his way. Producer Rick Berman discussed the concept with Roddenberry following his pushback, and the creator ended up folding on the plot point. The decision changed Klingon history forever in the canon of "Star Trek," but the creative disagreement highlighted how out of touch Roddenberry had become — and how his influence over the canon had declined over the 30-plus years he had been shaping the franchise. Years later, the iconic character would prove his staying power and Worf would appear in "Star Trek: Picard" in 2023.
entry.summary: Star Trek's Gene Roddenberry Tried To Kill A Major TNG Storyline Because Of One Character TVLine

entry.title: RHOA's Phaedra Parks finally confirms new romance with 'Traitors' costar - USA Today
entry.body: RHOA's Phaedra Parks finally confirms new romance with 'Traitors' costar The "Real Housewives of Atlanta" star says her “castle daddy” is more than a friend – and she’ll be CT Tamburello’s date at the Creative Arts Emmys. It's a "Traitors" love story. "Real Housewives of Atlanta" veteran Phaedra Parks, 52, confirmed that she is dating "The Challenge" star CT Tamburello, 46, on a Sept. 4 episode of SiriusXM’s "Jeff Lewis Live." After host Jeff Lewis asked the attorney and legal analyst if her relationship with Tamburello was platonic, she kept her response short and sweet: "No, it's not." At first, she only confirmed she was seeing someone named "CT," before a radio listener phoned in to connect the dots and ask if it was her "castle daddy" from "The Traitors" Season 2, which she and Tamburello competed in. However, she decided to keep the details of their relationship minimal, only teasing, "I can't give this to you. I've gotta save it for the world." She later confirmed that she will be Tamburello's date to the Creative Arts Emmy Awards on Saturday, Sept. 5, where he will present an award alongside his "Challenge" costar Johnny "Bananas" Devenanzio, who also appeared on "Traitors." Elsewhere in the interview, the reality star revealed she has been seeing Tamburello romantically since around the time of her last appearance on "Jeff Lewis Live," which was on Aug. How did Phaedra Parks and CT Tamburello meet? However, the two's history goes back to Season 2 of the Emmy-winning reality competition series "The Traitors," which premiered in January 2024 and was filmed in Scotland in late 2023. In the murder mystery, Parks competed as a traitor working with "Big Brother" alum Dan Gheesling, "Survivor" alum Parvati Shallow and "Below Deck" alum Kate Chastain to deceive and "murder" the faithful. She made it to seventh place before being banished in the penultimate episode by the remaining faithful, which included Tamburello. "I'm voting for Phaedra," Tamburello said during Season 2 while banishing Parks at the roundtable. "I think you came here to be the opposite of who you are in real life, and I think you've been the best traitor we've seen yet." Tamburello and fellow "Challenge" alum Trishelle Cannatella became the first two faithful players to win "The Traitors" after successfully being the last two standing. Throughout the season, Parks and Tamburello interacted playfully, with Parks calling him her "castle daddy," prompting many fans to speculate they were flirting and others to make video edits shipping them on social media.

entry.title: US envoys set for Ukraine talks after meeting Putin in Russia
entry.body: US envoys set for Ukraine talks after meeting Putin in Russia - Published Two US envoys are hoping for "equally productive meetings" in Ukraine after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on ending the war, US officials say. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to land in Kyiv on Sunday, having "discussed substantive plans for next steps" with Putin on Saturday, according to the White House. It is not yet clear exactly what they are, but an announcement is expected in the coming weeks, as efforts to end the war in Ukraine gather pace. It will be to the first trip by US President Donald Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital. Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days. As Witkoff and Kushner were negotiating at the Kremlin, Zelensky said he was ready for "a substantive conversation". Saturday's talks in Moscow lasted three hours and were held behind closed doors in Putin's official residence in the heart of the Russian capital, according to Russian state media. Details are still emerging, but both sides have given broadly positive remarks without going into specifics. Putin adviser Yuri Ushakov described the talks as "constructive, extremely frank". "The talks were not limited to an exchange of views on resolving the Ukrainian crisis - economic issues and potential major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects were discussed in considerable detail," he said. Ushakov also said "note was made of the Russian army's tangible advances in the combat zone" and that there was acknowledgement that talks needed to address "the root causes of the conflict". Despite an escalation of Russian missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian cities including Kyiv, Russian ground forces have made very slow advances for most of the conflict, incurring enormous casualties. Russia still controls about one-fifth of Ukrainian territory - areas that it seized back in 2022. Kushner and Witkoff have visited Russia several times but given Ukraine's airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, it is not clear how they will be travelling to Kyiv from Moscow. The talks come after Russia and Ukraine have intensified aerial attacks in recent months. Ukraine says it has struggled to repel ballistic missile attacks due to a lack of interceptor missiles, while Kyiv has focused its strikes on Russian economic infrastructure targets, notably oil installations. - Published6 hours ago - Published30 December 2025
entry.summary: It will be the first trip by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Trump's top negotiators, to Kyiv.

entry.title: German voters head to polls as far-right AfD party eyes historic state win - Al Jazeera
entry.body: Germans vote in eastern state as far-right AfD eyes power Saxony-Anhalt elections could see AfD become the first far-right party to take power at a state level since WWII. Voting is under way in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt that could see the Alternative for Germany (AfD) become the first far-right party to take power at a state level since World War II. Recent surveys place AfD at 40 percent, ahead of the centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU) at 23 percent. Recommended Stories list of 3 items - list 1 of 3Germany’s far right AfD eyes election breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt - list 2 of 3Germany’s far-right AfD eyes historic first in state election - list 3 of 3Thousands protest in Germany as far-right AfD party meets AfD has led comfortably in the pre-election opinion polls for months and has a chance at winning an absolute majority if several smaller parties fail to clear the 5 percent threshold to enter the parliament. A CDU-led administration under incumbent state premier Sven Schulze is the most likely outcome if the AfD does not win a majority. Weeks of coalition talks could follow the vote, depending on which parties surpass the 5 percent minimum. AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund, who was previously a member of the CDU, predicted gaining an absolute majority that would lead the anti-establishment party to national victory in 2029. He was named “Germany’s most dangerous man” by the influential magazine Der Spiegel. “It was the others who erected the firewalls,” he told German tabloid Bild. “If no one wants to work with us, then we’ll just have to do it alone.” An absolute majority would allow AfD to bypass mainstream parties’ “firewall” noncooperation policy, which the far-right party has already done at the local level. For the AfD, the Saxony-Anhalt elections are a stepping stone towards its larger ambition: securing national power in the 2029 federal elections. The CDU is led by deeply unpopular German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. At a local campaign rally in Lower Saxony a week before the election, Merz urged other politicians to engage with AfD more effectively. “We must address the issues at hand. We must also address our choice of words,” Merz said, referring to a statement by the AfD’s state leader in Saxony-Anhalt, Martin Reichardt. Reichardt previously told the AfD’s youth organisation that Germany had become “a lazy, anti-social bum reeking of dope”. Thousands of demonstrators gathered for a festival in support of democracy the night before the crucial election. Rally organisers estimated that between 15,000 and 20,000 people attended the demonstration. Initial results are expected at about 16:00 GMT (6pm local time) on Sunday.
entry.summary: German voters head to polls as far-right AfD party eyes historic state win Al Jazeera Germany’s far-right AfD is poised for power – and split on whether to cozy up to Trump CNN Germany’s Far Right Heads for Historic State Win: What to Watch Bloomberg.com The Ex-Salesman Bringing the Far Right to the Cusp of Power in Germany The New York Times Saxony-Anhalt's state election will have a nationwide impact DW.com

entry.title: Volcano eruption triggers flight suspensions at Indonesia's main airport
entry.body: Volcano eruption triggers flight suspensions at Indonesia's main airport - Published A volcanic eruption has halted hundreds of flights at Indonesia's main international airport, stranding tens of thousands of passengers. Authorities said 209 flights were suspended after ash from Anak Krakatau was detected in airspace near Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Sunday morning. The volcano had started erupting late on Friday night, generating continuous seismic activity, lava fountains, and booming sounds across surrounding regions. Two more eruptions happened early on Sunday, authorities said. More than 22,000 people have been impacted by the suspension of flights, which has been extended until 13:30 (0630 GMT). The transport ministry said the pause in operations mainly affected flights to and from Singapore, also other international routes including Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur. Authorities have confirmed there is no tsunami warning linked to the recent activity of the volcano, which is in the Sunda Strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra. The health minister has urged residents in affected areas to stay indoors and wear face masks to protect against respiratory, eye, and skin risks. According to local newspaper Kompas, several schools cancelled activities on Saturday after students and residents reported eye irritations from the ash, while some fishermen had cancelled fishing trips at sea similarly reporting sore eyes. One resident, Aldi Candra Prayogi, told the outlet that he felt since Friday evening and it felt like "small grains of sand had gotten into my eyes", and that he needs to use eye drops to ease the irritation. The dust is so thick that he has to sweep the front yard of his house every five minutes, he also said. Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatoa, has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatoa. The volcano - also known as Anak Krakatoa - collapsed in December 2018, triggering a huge tsunami which killed over 400 people, and displaced and injured thousands more on the nearby coastlines of Sumatra and Java. Scientists found that some of the chunks of rock that slid from the volcano when it collapsed were about 70-90m high. Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where there is high volcanic and seismic activity because of a line of frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions that circles virtually the entire Pacific rim. Related topics - Published2 October 2019 - Published24 December 2018
entry.summary: More than 20,000 passengers are stranded after ash was detected in airspace near Jakarta following the eruptions.

entry.title: Fuel tanker blast in western Iran kills at least 10 - Al Jazeera
entry.body: Fuel tanker blast in western Iran kills at least 10 At least six other people were injured in the tanker blast on Iran’s Hamedan-Sanandaj highway, officials say. At least 10 people were killed in a fuel tanker blast in western Iran, Iranian national broadcast media (IRIB) reported. The tanker explosion on Saturday was triggered by a road crash on the Hamedan-Sanandaj highway. Recommended Stories list of 3 items - list 1 of 3US-Iran ceasefire? Not for Indian sailors being killed in Hormuz - list 2 of 3Diesel price hits all-time high in US amid Iran war woes - list 3 of 3Trump calls Iran war ‘small potatoes’, compares US deaths with Vietnam war The accident was caused by a technical fault in the braking system of the vehicle carrying the tanker, said the governor of Sanandaj, the capital of Iran’s Kurdistan province, as reported by the Reuters news agency. At least six other people were injured in the incident, the governor also said, adding that casualty figures were based on initial reports. According to local officials, the resulting fire was immediately brought under control. They did not provide further details on the identities of those killed. The latest deadly accident adds to a long history of deadly tanker and bus collisions in Iran, where poor road conditions, ageing vehicle fleets and heavy freight traffic have made such accidents a recurring hazard. At least 13 people were killed in 2018, after a fuel tanker slammed into a bus that had stopped to pick up passengers near Sanandaj. UNICEF said Iran’s rate of traffic crashes is 20 times the world’s average, as the country suffers from poor roads and lax traffic enforcement. According to a May 2017 report by the Tehran-based newspaper Financial Tribune, more than 20,000 people are killed and 800,000 are injured annually in road accidents in Iran.

entry.title: Washington blocks new Trump mail voting rules, keeping midterm election procedures intact - komonews.com
entry.body: Washington blocks new Trump mail voting rules, keeping midterm election procedures intact OLYMPIA, Wash. — With the midterm election approaching, the future of mail-in voting remains tied up in court, but a recent ruling means Washington state’s voting process will stay the same for November. In March, President Donald Trump signed an executive order to restrict mail-in voting, setting off an ongoing legal battle. RELATED | Washington sees 32% jump in ballots rejected for late postmarks after USPS rule change Most recently, the U.S. Postal Service posted new rules for mail-in voting to comply with the executive order. The rules would have required changes including a new envelope with a barcode for mail-in ballots. Washington state, along with 25 other states, filed a lawsuit arguing the changes the USPS was demanding would be too difficult to achieve before the upcoming election. District Judge Indira Talwani extended her initial preliminary injunction, temporarily pausing enforcement of the new rules while the case is sorted out. Secretary of State Steve Hobbs said the midterm election in Washington will be safe, secure, and accessible. Ballots for the midterm election will start being mailed out Oct.

entry.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy links Russian strikes on Kyiv airports to US envoys’ visit - The Guardian
entry.body: - Russian attacks on Kyiv and Boryspil international airports were “clearly” a reaction to the possibility of the US negotiators flying to Kyiv after talks in Moscow, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has said. On Saturday, Zelenskyy said Kyiv had “taken note of this Russian move, and next week we will adjust our operation accordingly regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous because of our drones and missiles in the sky. Of course, there are and will be no threats to diplomacy from our side.” Both airports service the Ukrainian capital. - There was no comment from the US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who were visiting Moscow for the first time since January. They flew out of Moscow soon after the talks and were due to meet Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday. The Kremlin’s tone appeared unchanged. After three hours of talks, an aide to Vladimir Putin, Yuri Ushakov, said the Russian president had told the US pair that Russia was making “real progress” on the battlefield, was confident of achieving its goals, and stressed the necessity of addressing “all the root causes of the conflict”. Ushakov said the Americans had “outlined a number of ideas regarding possible avenues for a settlement”, but he did not say what those ideas were. - The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250km (775-mile) frontline. Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov posted online that Putin had ordered the military not to strike Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight on Saturday. However, he said Russia had not yet agreed to a broader three-day ceasefire. Zelenskyy has said Ukraine is prepared to refrain from strikes on Moscow through to Monday. - Russian attacks killed five employees and wounded five others at an industrial facility in the Dnipropetrovsk region, said the local military administration head, Oleksandr Hanzha. “A locksmith, an electrician, a plumber and a machinist. They were simply working their shift. They were doing their job when enemy missiles cut off their lives.” Russia’s defence ministry said it had carried out strikes on two metallurgical plants that it claimed were sites for military production. - A 62-year-old man was wounded, and several homes and an apartment building damaged, in a separate attack on the region’s Nikopol district, Hanzha said. The city of Dnipro and the nearby Pidhorodne community were among the areas hit. One person died and five other were injured, including two men who were hospitalised in serious condition. A sixth civilian was injured in an attack on the Nikopol district. - Other deadly Russian attacks took place in Chuhuiv in Ukraine’s eastern Kharkiv region, on the Bucha district of Ukraine’s Kyiv region, and on a shopping centre in the southern Mykolaiv region. In Russia’s Belrogod region on the border with Ukraine, two people were killed and three others wounded by Ukrainian attacks on Saturday, local authorities said. Russia launched ballistic missiles from its Rostov and Voronezh regions and deployed 167 attack drones, Ukraine’s air force said on Saturday.
entry.summary: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy links Russian strikes on Kyiv airports to US envoys’ visit The Guardian At least 5 killed in Russian attacks on Ukraine as US envoys visit Moscow Al Jazeera Russia Strikes Ukrainian Airports, Infrastructure Ahead of U.S. Envoys' Visit The Moscow Times Russia Strikes Abandoned Soviet-Era Planes in Kyiv to Send a Signal to the US, Lawmaker Says UNITED24 Media Zelenskyy: Russia strikes airports in Zhuliany and Boryspil pravda.com.ua

entry.title: Natalie Imbruglia on her worst audition: 'I remember feeling icky'
entry.body: Natalie Imbruglia on her worst audition: 'I remember feeling icky' - Published When it comes to writing music, Natalie Imbruglia needs constant motion. "I walk around in circles to get the melodies, to catch them," the Australian singer says. "If I'm sat in a chair, I get nothing. "So if I go and work with someone new and they have a shoebox-sized studio, I'm like, 'How am I going to do my circles?'" Imbruglia doesn't know exactly how many laps she completed during the making of her dancefloor-ready seventh album, Algorithm. But it was a lot. Inspired by Talking Heads and Grace Jones, it's a record whose shimmering surfaces disguise lyrics of deep emotional complexity. On Who Dimmed The Lights, the 51-year-old addresses how her mental health "unravelled" as she went through perimenopause. "It was really tough," she says. "Perimenopause is not just about hormones. It's to do with your mind. Your brain needs oestrogen to function, so when the levels fluctuate, it affects your spatial awareness. "I've never walked into so many doorways. The brain fog's quite jarring." Doorways weren't the only problem. Imbruglia says perimenopause exacerbated her ADHD, which she was diagnosed with in midlife. Other symptoms included heightened anxiety and anger. "You start seeing an expression on other people of, like, 'What's happening to you?' "I was seeing that face a lot, and it's to do with your ability to process [information]. Your fuse is shorter." Things came to a head on tour, where her stage fright went into overdrive and she suffered "just terrible, terrible anxiety". "I become sensitive to sound, so it feels like you're screaming at me if you're talking normally," she says. "I can't process questions very well. I act twitchy and weird, and it seemed to get worse with perimenopause." She says her behaviour became a "nightmare" for her team. Pressed for an example, she explains: "If you asked me whether I wanted still or sparkling water, I'd say, 'That's a question, and I can't answer questions right now'. "How diva is that?" Well, it's not exactly Mariah Carey demanding baskets of puppies and forbidding eye contact, but Imbruglia was shaken up. The day after one concert, she told her co-writers David Sneddon and Anu Pillai, "Guys, I think I'm going to have to quit my job because I can't cope with how I'm treating people before the show." They helped to talk her down, putting her fight-or-flight instincts into context. "What they helped me realise is that I was trying to stop the behaviour with willpower, and if I just relaxed into it and said to myself, 'You know, you're about to perform in front of a lot of people, it's natural that you're nervous', maybe I wouldn't be resisting it as much." The impromptu therapy session inspired a new song, Upside Down, external - but Imbruglia is understandably frustrated that perimenopause isn't more widely understood, saying many women are rejected by their GP when they seek HRT treatment. "My mum never talked to me about it," she reflects, "but looking back, I know she had a really bad one. "Her anxiety was off the charts, too, and I have a lot more compassion now, because she had four kids. I've only got one." As a child in Sydney, Imbruglia was drawn to performing. She'd squeeze lemon on her hair to make it blonder, and put on concerts of Whitney Houston covers for her neighbours. Before long, she was cast in commercials for Coca-Cola and Twisties, and spent her Christmases singing carols in shopping centres. "But when you turn 15 or 16, and you're into boys, you're like, 'Oh, that's really naff. I don't want to be doing that any more'," she laughs. From that point onwards, Imbruglia became "basically unparentable". "I was sneaking out and sleeping in someone's car on the beach, then getting busted. "My parents were really strict - and my mum would turn up at parties with my picture, going, 'Have you seen this girl?' "Socially, it was a disaster." Music continued to be her solace. Dating a drummer, she switched allegiance from Whitney Houston to Tom Waits and Tori Amos, but the urge to sing remained. You can see that hunger in a recently rediscovered photograph of a pre-fame Imbruglia, external, pressed up against the barriers of an INXS concert in 1992. "It was my first ever concert," she says. I had white, tight jeans on." In the photo, "everyone else is screaming but I'm looking at (Michael Hutchence) with this determination in my eyes. "I'm studying him, like, 'How can I be up there too?'" She got her chance in 1997 after quitting her role as builder's apprentice Beth Brennan in Aussie soap Neighbours. Moving to London, she signed a deal with RCA Records and immediately scored an international hit with her first single, Torn. Famously, the song was a cover â a fact journalists never let her forget, even though she co-wrote every other track on her debut album, Left of the Middle (lifetime sales, seven million copies). "Yeah, I got famous on a song that I didn't write," she says now, "but there's more to what you bring to a song than whether you wrote the lyrics." She still loves the song â "Torn was a beautiful gift" â but the furore around it fuelled her insecurities. As a result, she essentially self-sabotaged her career. The lead single from her second album, That Day, was a free-verse stream-of-consciousness that sounded like a manic inner monologue. "That was my rebellion against Torn," she says. "It doesn't have a chorus. "That was my way of going, 'Can I get on with my life now? I've just started learning the craft of songwriting, I'm young, I didn't ask for this'." In the midst of the madness, she auditioned for the lead role of Satine in Baz Luhrmann's Moulin Rouge â which counts as one of the stranger experiences of her career. "The audition was, pretty much, 'Have an orgasm'," she grimaces. "Because I think that happens in the movie." (Indeed, Satine delivers a breathy boudoir monologue, external as she tries to seduce Ewan McGregor's character, Christian.) But Imbruglia stresses it wasn't a creepy casting couch situation. "It's Baz, that doesn't really fit," she says of the soft-hearted director. "But I remember leaving and feeling really icky. Like, 'Ohhh, that was awful. Where's my mummy?'" Back in the world of music, Imbruglia returned to more commercial sounds on hits like Wrong Impression (2002) and Shiver (2005). But sales dwindled and her fourth album was shelved by her label. In the years that followed, she joined the Australian version of The X Factor and appeared in a UK production of Alan Ayckbourn's play Things We Do for Love, before making a tentative return to music with covers album Male (2015); and the more personal, introspective Firebird (2021). "It was quitting music and coming back to it that gave me an appreciation of my abilities," she says. "I might not be the best songwriter, even now, but there's only one me, and when I go inside myself and feel the emotion of what I'm writing about and deliver it, that's what my fans resonate with, and that's enough." She certainly has a lot to say on Algorithm. As well as the frank discussion of mental health, the title track talks about her flirtation with internet conspiracy theories. She won't say which ones ("I think it's irresponsible") but stresses the danger is omnipresent. "There's a voice in my head that says, 'You don't want to click on that', and I'll click on it. "You have to change the settings. Don't allow yourself to be in a situation where your stress relief is scrolling on a phone in bed. It's just not healthy." Ultimately, however, the album ends on a note of positivity. Beautiful Love, external, co-written with Snow Patrol's Gary Lightbody, is a soaring hymn to embracing your flaws and making peace with life's highs and lows. "I've always made the joke that I'll never be a Buddhist because it's a middle path," she smiles. "I like the pendulum to swing. Whether it's extreme joy or extreme pain, I like to feel the experience of life." Related topics - Published7 July 2022
entry.summary: The pop star's first album since 2021 deals with the mental health fallout of perimenopause.

entry.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming's new hourly cap is reportedly set exactly where Microsoft stops making money on it - Eurogamer.net
entry.body: Xbox Cloud Gaming's new hourly cap is reportedly set exactly where Microsoft stops making money on it Break, even. Xbox announced hard monthly time limits will be added to its cloud gaming streaming service earlier this week, with time limits coming into effect for all three tiers of Xbox Game Pass subscription. According to Windows Central, which cites unnamed Microsoft sources, that's not an arbitrary cap and is, allegedly, set at Microsoft's own break-even threshold as any usage beyond that costs the company money. Windows Central ties the cost pressure to a wider squeeze on server memory caused by Microsoft's AI investments, with Azure capacity increasingly prioritised for AI workloads over game streaming. It frames the caps as part of a broader cost-cutting pattern across Xbox, alongside recent layoffs and cancelled projects, as the division comes under pressure to turn a bigger profit. As Connor reported for us in the week, according to a 2025 report from Statista, US gamers spent an average of 9.5 hours per week playing video games, UK gamers 6.38 hours, and a worldwide average of 6.56 hours was recorded. Despite Xbox scaling back its cloud gaming plans and the seemingly endless issues caused by the ramping up of AI data centres, industry giants remain bullish on cloud gaming. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said he believed we'd all be streaming our games in about "three years" in a recent financial report, while Xbox rolled out an ad-supported game streaming test for its insider programs. This comes amid a hardware crisis where the cost of buying consoles and gaming PCs has become increasingly less affordable, potentially leaving streaming the sole option for many in the future despite its issues.

entry.title: iPhone Handoff will seamlessly share one number between two phones - The Verge
entry.body: When iOS 27 lands later this month, it will have a feature called iPhone Handoff that lets you switch between two phones using the same number. It was briefly mentioned during the WWDC keynote back in June, but there were no details at the time. Now there’s a demo clip showing how to set up the feature running in Xcode 27’s Device Hub. It lets you pair two iPhones, using one as your main device and the other as its “companion.” iPhone Handoff will seamlessly share one number between two phones The feature is expected to launch as part of iOS 27 later this month. Launching the feature now makes sense with the expected launch of the foldable iPhone Ultra right around the corner. People might not always want to take a chunky and extremely expensive device out with them. So Handoff would let users temporarily switch over to a cheaper, smaller device — like that cracked iPhone 13 you’ve been stubbornly refusing to upgrade. The feature will require carrier support, however. References to T-Mobile US and Telekom.de were found in the code, but support beyond that is unknown.

entry.title: No, Sony isn't cutting PlayStation disc production by 90 percent, just 10 - Eurogamer.net
entry.body: Sony clarifies PlayStation disc production is dropping by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent Spin doctors. Sony has pushed back on a wave of reports suggesting PlayStation disc manufacturing is about to be gutted by 90 percent after comments from a Sony DADC executive were allegedly misunderstood. According to Game, which went directly to Sony Digital Audio Disc Corporation (DADC) for clarity, output is actually expected to dip by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent. "To clarify and avoid any misleading information: in that statement Dietmar anticipated an overall product volume decline by 10 percent, not a decline down to 10 percent," a Sony DADC spokesperson told Game, referring to comments made by DADC chief Dietmar Tanzer to an Austrian broadcaster in July. The spokesperson didn't say what happens beyond 2028, and directed further questions on reorders to PlayStation's own PR team, which didn't respond to Game's queries. The confusion stems from PlayStation's July announcement that it will stop producing physical discs for new games from January 2028 onward, though already-released titles and games still slated for disc release before that date aren't affected, and reorders will continue afterwards. Unlike Microsoft, which certifies third-party "Authorised Replicators" to press Xbox discs under its publisher agreements, Sony keeps disc manufacturing in-house, running it through DADC rather than opening the process up to outside plants. Niko Partners analyst Daniel Ahmad posited that cutting discs kills the resale market outright and pulls spending straight into the PlayStation Store, where Sony's margins are considerably better than they are on a retail sale. Shawn Layden, the former chairman of SIE Worldwide Studios, told Game a disc-free future for PlayStation is "depressing, but solvable", though he said he doesn't have "line of sight on the particulars" of any potential licensing deal. He compared the situation to other physical media formats that outlasted predictions of their demise. "No one ever saw the comeback of cassette tape. And vinyl didn't so much come back. The flame went down, the fire's dying, but the ember was always there, and it just kind of came back. Much like the book business. We thought we'd all be on Kindles right now". For Layden, collecting is core to what makes someone a gamer in the first place. "Did you get all the diamonds in Crash Bandicoot? Did you get all the stars in Mario? And we like to collect our games. And we have a game shelf. And we put all our boxes up there. And if you're super hardcore, when you buy a game, you buy two copies, right? One stays in the shrink wrap, and you play the other one. "You know, we buy the steelbook and the three-disc Final Fantasy set and the figurine and, you know, you can't download any of that. What happens to that?" He argued that decisions like this get treated as pure financial calculations when they shouldn't be. "Someone also has to have a ledger there saying, 'OK, what is the brand impact from that move?'" he said. "If we do that, dollars and cents work out. But what's the brand impact? Are people going to say, 'Good move, you guys?' Or are they going to say, 'We hate you guys. Quit doing that.' And sometimes they say, 'We hate you'." He added: "I see a lot of companies making decisions which, objectively speaking, I don't know what the dollar end of that was for you, Mr. Company, but your brand value just dropped 30 percent. So I hope it was worth it". On the broader shift away from physical ownership, Layden was blunt. "What does ownership mean anymore? Well, in fact, it's not even a question anymore. It's like you are shifting the model from ownership to accessibility. "You've never been able to sell your iTunes library. And you can't sell your PlayStation download library. So if you can't resell it, do you really own it?" Boutique publisher iam8bit, known for collector's editions, told Game it would "absolutely love to find a way forward to continue making physical PlayStation games". One possible route floated in the piece is Conectiv Supply Chain Solutions, a Memphis-based disc manufacturer formed in 2025 that recently acquired Universal and Warner Bros' home entertainment distributor SDS, though Game reported it hadn't heard back from the company or its CEO by the time of publication. Earlier this week, messages like "NO DISC NO BUY" and "WE WANT DESTINY 3" were spammed during the State of Play, from start to finish, in the YouTube live chat. Popping over the Twitch, that stream was endlessly spammed by Destiny emotes, and similar calls for physical game support. This outrage is a collision between two separate PR disasters for Sony. The first is tied to Sony's announcement that physical game support will stop starting in 2028, meaning only digital codes will be available for games on its platform starting in January of that year. The second controversy stems from the end of major support for Destiny 2 and major staffing cuts at Bungie.
entry.summary: No, Sony isn't cutting PlayStation disc production by 90 percent, just 10 Eurogamer.net Sony's PlayStation disc plant is losing 10 percent of its volume in 2028, not 90 Substack PlayStation State Of Play Hijacked By ‘Destiny 3,’ Physical Disc Demands Forbes After a Record Breaking State of Play in June, the Latest Edition Did Disappointing Numbers Push Square Sony's digital-only future will hit 62% of the world the hardest, and nobody is talking about it XDA

entry.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Passes 1 Million Copies Sold in Just 2 Days - IGN
entry.body: Single-player RPG and new IP The Blood of Dawnwalker has sold 1 million copies just two days after its launch, publisher Bandai Namco and developer Rebel Wolves have announced. Official social media accounts for the first-time developer's new game confirmed the news with a celebratory graphic today. The milestone was reached just 48 hours after The Blood of Dawnwalker launched for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 3. "Thank you for playing, sharing, supporting, and being part of the community!" Rebel Wolves said in a message to fans. Thank you for playing, sharing, supporting, and being part of the community! ❤ pic.twitter.com/9fNqO8gNGB — Dawnwalker (@DawnwalkerGame) September 5, 2026 An official summary for The Blood of Dawnwalker describes it as an "open-world dark fantasy action RPG set in 14th-century Europe." In this first chapter, players take the role of Coen, a "human by day and vampire by night" who is fighting for his family in a narrative shaped by player choice. It also happens to have an in-game clock that sees Coen's story take place through a 30-day period. It's something some players love – and others don't. Reaching 1 million copies sold in such a short amount of time would be an impressive feat for any game, but there are a few reasons it's especially noteworthy for the Rebel Wolves team. This is the studio's first major release since it was founded in 2022. Led by The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt director and Cyberpunk 2077 co-director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, The Blood of Dawnwalker is also a new IP. The Warsaw-based studio previously released a CGI teaser to tease how sequels could potentially expand on its dark fantasy formula in new and interesting ways. "The CGI teaser shows where the dark fantasy saga is heading," Bandai Namco said in a June press release. "Players can see Coen in completely different surroundings than the ones they are used to – a modern, 21st-century setting, offering a glimpse of where the overarching plot ultimately leads. As the developers revealed, the next installments of the Dawnwalker franchise will span centuries, continents, and cultures across the globe." Surreal. Thank you so much!🔥🙏 https://t.co/qhrBwsfOlv — Mateusz Tomaszkiewicz 🧛♂️ (@MTomaszkiewicz) September 5, 2026 Speechless. Tearing up a little 🥹 We're a passionate bunch. And we're not stopping here 😤 Thank you for trusting us ❤️ https://t.co/FCRMmJCBbP Tomaszkiewicz said at the time that each installment in the Dawnwalker series is planned to be a standalone entry "with its own story, without narrative cliffhangers, unresolved plot threads, or time travel ideas." With 1 million copies in players' hands out of the gate, those sequels already feel more likely to materialize. Although the when and where for these planned follow-ups have yet to be revealed, narrative director Jakub Szamałek has at least told fans to keep an eye out for "breadcrumbs related to the overarching plot spanning the saga" in The Blood of Dawnwalker. It helps that Rebel Wolves secured solid reviews upon the launch of its first game. IGN, for example, called it "amazing" in our 9/10 review. We said, "The Blood of Dawnwalker is an impressive, bloody cocktail of interesting ideas and well-written characters, making it one of this year’s best open-world RPGs." We'll have to wait to see what updates Bandai Namco and Rebel Wolves have in store. In the meantime, you can read what Tomaszkiewicz had to tell us when it comes to the studio's plans to establish even more new IP. For everything you need to know before starting the game yourself, click here. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

entry.title: Taylor's 'dream ending to a dream career'
entry.body: Taylor's 'dream ending to a dream career' - Published "There's nothing like an Irish family." Katie Taylor addressed the Croke Park crowd as she paid tribute to her mother Bridget, but her extended family of 83,000 inside Croke Park and many more tuning in will have known this one was for them too. Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Taylor is no ordinary fighter and her swansong proved as extraordinary as the fighter and person. After 30 years lacing up the gloves, Taylor, 40, sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells in front of 83,000 adoring fans at Dublin's iconic Croke Park, just three miles from the scene of her first official bout 25 years earlier. The final act in the ring was to sweep past Flora Pili to cement her legacy in Ireland and beyond, bowing out as a three-time and two-weight undisputed champion. It was a night of celebration, cheers and plenty of tears as fans and peers turned out for her victory lap, showing love and appreciation for a career which thrilled and inspired in equal measure. "It was everything I expected and more," Taylor said at her final post-fight news conference. "Thankfully I was able to hold my emotions together tonight as I was getting emotional all week and the last few months' preparation was so emotional. "The atmosphere was so special. I was beyond my wildest dreams - what a special night." - Taylor crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph - Published9 hours ago - Tears, blood & triumph - Taylor's iconic career in pictures - Published8 hours ago Before her hand could be raised in the ring, there were battles to be won outside of it. Born in 1986 as the youngest of four children to former Irish champion father Peter and mother Bridget - one of Ireland's first female officials - the very notion of women's boxing in Ireland appeared fanciful. While older brothers Lee and Peter were welcomed into the boxing fold, Katie became K from Bray - a girl hiding her identity to simply compete in an exclusively male environment. The fighting spirit and determination which characterises her sporting prowess is as much a feature of her personality, and in 2001 as a 15-year-old she took part in the first sanctioned women's bout in Ireland since it was outlawed following future world champion Deirdre Gogarty's 1991 debut in Limerick. Perhaps fitting, as five years earlier, Taylor wrote to role model Gogarty, expressing frustration at the lack of opportunities to compete and outlining her dreams of one day being allowed to compete at the Olympic Games. Prophetic words, as it was her exceptional talent on display in front of International Olympic Committee members in 2007 which convinced them to add women's boxing to the programme for London 2012. All eyes were on her as Katie mania grew throughout the Games - her victory over Sofya Ochigava in the lightweight final a moment of national sporting joy comparable to the heady days of Jack Charlton's Republic of Ireland teams at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups - the Excel arena transformed into a small corner of Ireland on an unforgettable day. A recognised star in Irish boxing circles was now a household name, her humble and gracious manner winning the hearts of a nation that has remained firmly in her corner. "The 'ole ole oles' carried me all over the world: to Leeds, to Manchester, Brooklyn, Boston, Dallas, Manhattan," she reflected. "This night is so special because I wanted to put on a performance for them. I don't think it was a career-best performance, but I got the win for them, just to say 'thank you'." A seminal night against Serrano Her star did not dim despite a disappointing Rio Games in 2016, and while Matchroom boss Eddie Hearn took convincing to take a punt on her as a professional, the faith has been repaid in spades. Within three years, Taylor was undisputed champion at lightweight, rising from undercard to centre stage as she carried out her promise to do for women's professional boxing what she had achieved as an amateur, all to a chorus of the aforementioned 'ole ole oles' from the support which followed her every move. A seminal night in 2022 saw her defeat Amanda Serrano at a sold-out Madison Square Garden in a fight of the year contender - the first time a women's bout had headlined the famous arena, a major turning point for the female code. They would trade leather a further two times after Taylor had avenged her sole professional career defeat by Chantelle Cameron to become a two-weight champion. Perhaps that was the perfect way to sign off, but the Croke Park itch had to be scratched and while those gates seemed destined to remain locked, Taylor's status made it happen. Could she fill such a vast stadium? Perhaps the doubters did not grasp the reverence in which the softly spoken yet inspirational woman from Bray is held. While her trophy cabinet is overflowing with gold medals and world title belts, perhaps her greatest legacy is leaving women's boxing in a vastly better place than she found it - that Serrano trilogy lifting women's boxing to new heights. Taylor broke through the barriers with a grace which belied the obstacles she faced yet her quiet determination and humble nature will serve as an example of what can be achieved by belief, hard work and a refusal to accept her lot as young girls can now walk the path she laid. Fierce inside the ring yet unassuming outside of it - even factoring in an impulse-buy speedboat, since sold - superlatives such as trailblazer, icon and Ireland's greatest sportsperson are not hyperbolic, for Taylor's status as a legend is in no way cliched. She has indicated she will remain in the sport, but for now, there is time to savour an extraordinary career, with her place among boxing's greats set in stone. Irish boxing is going to be a lesser place. "I'm retired now so I can eat what I want, but I'm just going to enjoy a nice celebration and look back on a dream ending to a dream career. "My story is the story of everyone in this room: we all have our ups and downs. I think people resonate with your vulnerabilities and your successes - saw me cope with the heartbreak of Rio, the Chantelle Cameron loss and personal difficulties. "My story is the story of everyone in this room." Related topics - Published3 days ago - Published22 August - Published28 April 2024 More boxing from the BBC - Published28 August
entry.summary: Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Irish icon Katie Taylor sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells at Dublin's towering Croke Park.

entry.title: 'I don't really want to talk' - Fritz and Cobolli shocked as seeds tumble
entry.body: Fritz and Cobolli shocked as men's seeds tumble - Published Taylor Fritz was unable to explain how he let a two-set lead slip against Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo as he became one of six top-10 seeds to be eliminated from the men's draw in the first week of the US Open. The American ninth seed was in complete control and went an early break up in the third set, only for 24th seed Cerundolo to produce a shock 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4 win to reach the fourth round. Less than an hour later, fifth seed Flavio Cobolli of Italy fell to a 6-7 (4-7) 6-3 6-0 6-3 defeat by Belgium's Alexander Blockx, opening up the men's draw even further. However, German top seed Alexander Zverev did survive. The French Open champion won 6-2 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 against Chilean 25th seed Alejandro Tabilo to move into the last 16. "I don't even know what to say," Fritz said. "I don't really want to talk to anybody, see anybody. "I need to get out for a couple days and then get back to work. I don't know how I let that happen today." Fritz, a finalist at Flushing Meadows in 2024, was bidding to become the fifth American through to the fourth round at this year's tournament. With world number one Jannik Sinner out injured and Carlos Alcaraz only recently returned from a long-term wrist problem, excitement has been growing there may finally be another home winner in the men's singles - 23 years on from Andy Roddick's triumph. That chance remains with Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe, Tommy Paul, Alex Michelsen and Learner Tien left - but Fritz will know he has let a golden opportunity slip. Cerundolo and 28th seed Blockx will now meet in the fourth round with a place in the quarter-finals up for grabs. - Zheng goes from 5-0 and match point down to victory - Published9 hours ago - Gauff wins but mixed fortunes for home hopes at US Open - Published4 hours ago Cobolli exit clears path for Zverev The chance of a maiden Grand Slam title has also escaped Cobolli after his capitulation against Blockx. Having edged the first set on a tie-break, the Italian lost his way and could not recover after surrendering the third set to love in just 20 minutes. "I think my energy was a little bit lower than the other days," said the French Open finalist. "I feel a little bit more tight and maybe more tired." With Cobolli and Fritz out, Zverev and 14th seed Learner Tien - who completed a five-set win over Czech 17th seed Jakub Mensik at 1:35am in New York - are the only top-20 players left in the top half of the draw. It means Zverev could reach the final without playing a top-10 opponent. But first he must focus on getting past Italian 21st seed Luciano Darderi after seeing off Tabilo in another late-night finish. Zverev's opening two matches were five-set victories finishing around 2am, but this time he got the job done in straight sets at 1:09am local time. However, he had to save two set points to prevent Tabilo levelling the match at one-set all, and survived two break points early in the third set, before reasserting his authority. "My coach was smart because he explained to me that a best-of-five match doesn't mean you have to play five sets - which I didn't know until today," joked Zverev. "I'm happy with the improvements and happy my level is going in the right direction. But I can still play better." How the seeds have fallen This year's biggest shock at Flushing Meadows was also the first, as Novak Djokovic was beaten by Argentina's Mariano Navone on the opening day's play. Fourth seed Djokovic was eyeing an historic 25th Grand Slam title but was left in tears after a five-set loss to the world number 49. Next to go was 10th seed Arthur Fils. The Frenchman was another first-round casualty as he went down in four sets against former world number three Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece. The highest seed ousted thus far is Canada's Felix Auger-Aliassime, the third seed, who lost to Karen Khachanov in round two, the same stage at which sixth seed Alex de Minaur was beaten. Those exits looked to have cleared the way for Fritz and Cobolli to go deep into the tournament, but it was an opportunity neither were able to take. In the men's doubles, British pair Arthur Fery and Joshua Paris progressed with a 6-4 5-7 6-4 win over Anirudh Chandrasekar of India and Ivan Liutarevich of Belarus. Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison, the fifth seeds, also advanced as they beat French duo Arthur Reymond and Luca Sanchez 6-0 7-6 (7-3). But there was disappointment for David Stevenson and Marcus Willis as they lost 5-7 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 to France's 11th seeds Sadio Doumbia and Fabien Reboul. Related topics - Published28 August
entry.summary: Taylor Fritz and Flavio Cobolli lose in the third round as six top-10 seeds are knocked out of the men's singles in the first week at the US Open.

entry.title: Oklahoma State football embarrassed by Tulsa to start Eric Morris era: Replay, highlights - The Oklahoman
entry.body: Oklahoma State football embarrassed by Tulsa to start Eric Morris era: Replay, highlights Tre Lamb was right. It was around seven months ago when Tulsa’s football coach declared to Golden Hurricane fans that his team would “beat their a-- again” during their rematch with Oklahoma State. It felt a tad foolish with the new regime taking over in Stillwater. In what could be described as a true failure, the Cowboys were a mess in Eric Morris’ head coaching debut, falling 24-10 at Tulsa on Saturday. It’s the second straight season the Golden Hurricane upset the Cowboys, who opened the week as a two-touchdown favorite. Instead, the Pokes were fortunate to get into the end zone just once. The new-look offense led by quarterback Drew Mestemaker stalled, particularly on fourth-down plays. OSU was 2 of 6 on that down. Mestemaker was 29 of 49 for 241 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Running back Caleb Hawkins rushed for 79 yards on 18 carries. OSU’s defense was mostly solid and kept the Cowboys in the game, though it wore down in the second half as Tulsa started to pull away. The Golden Hurricane totaled 363 yards. And after Tulsa’s Damari Alston scored his second TD on a 29-yard rush with 7:52 left for a 24-10 lead, it was all but over. Then it was basically sealed when Zach Williams intercepted Mestemaker in the end zone with 4:13 remaining. That leaves a really sour taste in the mouths of the Cowboys as they go to Week 2 with a matchup against College Football Playoff contender Oregon. entry.title: Vikings' legend Harrison Smith returning to Minnesota on a one-year deal, per report - CBS Sports
entry.body: The Minnesota Vikings are bringing back former All-Pro safety Harrison Smith on a one-year, $12.25 million deal, according to NFL Media. A bonafide Vikings legend, the 37-year-old Smith will return to Minnesota for his 15th NFL season. During his first 14 seasons with the Vikings, Smith -- the 12th overall pick in the 2012 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame -- was a six-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro. Each of Smith's Pro Bowl nods took place from 2015-21. He was a first-team All-Pro in 2017 while helping the Vikings advance to within a game of the Super Bowl. Smith is renowned for his impressive production across the board. His 39 career interceptions are the most in the NFL among active players. He also has 1,180 career tackles (51 for loss), 21.5 sacks, 13 forced fumbles, 10 fumble recoveries, 106 pass breakups and four interception returns for scores. While he hasn't been named to a Pro Bowl since 2021, Smith has continued to be a productive player. In 15 games last season, Smith filled the stat sheet with two interceptions, 10 pass breakups, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery and 54 tackles. Smith will re-join a Vikings defense that invested heavily on the defensive side of the ball during April's draft. Minnesota drafted five defensive players that included first-round pick Caleb Banks and fellow defensive backs Jakobe Thomas and Charles Demmings. Minnesota opens the 2026 season home against the Packers on Sept.
