White commented on E! 4 Instagram post about the new couple with "Sign the papers" and three hands clapping emojis. "Soo much I could say right now because I know what really happened lol," Angelina Pivarnick of Jersey Shore Family Vacation commented on the same post. Thank you to the real trophy for making a beautiful night even better. #Emmys," Parks captioned the photos. "Yasssssss Frack," Porsha Williams commented. She was a faithful contestant on season 4 of The Traitors US. "He made it clear to her he really, really liked her and he fell for her when they were on Traitors," a source told Page Six. "They really do laugh together a lot and their relationship is really sweet," the insider later said. Tamburello posted a video of Parks getting her makeup done on his Instagram story with the words, "…how'd I get so lucky!?" over it. The next video was his "miracle workers" doing his makeup. He showed a short video of the Emmys audience and the announcement that Alan Cumming won for hosting the competition series for The Traitors US. Tamburello hasn't addressed his separation from White recently. entry.title: Witkoff and Kushner, in a first, visit Ukraine for peace talks
entry.body: President Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic talks aimed at resuming negotiations between Russia and Ukraine . Why it matters: Kushner and Witkoff traveled to Kyiv right after talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. This is Witkoff and Kushner's first trip to Ukraine despite months of negotiating with both sides and multiple trips to Russia. Sunday also marked the highest-level visit by a U.S. official to Ukraine since Trump started his second term. Driving the news: U.S. and Russian officials offered positive assessments of Kushner and Witkoff's three-hour meeting with Putin on Saturday. "Kushner and Witkoff are making an effort, and we are making progress," a Russian official said. A White House official said Witkoff, Kushner and Putin discussed "plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks." Witkoff, Kushner and their team left Moscow on Saturday night, landed several hours later in Poland, and then traveled by land to Kyiv. Zoom in: Zelensky discussed Ukrainian preparations for continuing the war through the winter, a source familiar with the meetings said. Kushner and Witkoff stressed they want a breakthrough before winter, the source said. Witkoff and Kushner met twice with Zelensky and his senior advisers. National security advisers from the U.K., France and Germany joined a third meeting. After the second meeting with Zelensky, Trump's envoys said they were "encouraged by the substantive discussion" and looked forward to making more progress. What they're saying: A second source who participated in Sunday's talks said the meetings "went well" and that Kushner and Witkoff want to work with the parties on a "refreshed" peace proposal. "Things may move in a good direction if there's a follow-up by all parties involved," the source said. Editor's note: This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

entry.title: Dem governors weighing White House face the DeSantis dilemma
entry.body: Top aides for Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis ' failed 2024 presidential campaign have a warning for Democratic governors eyeing a 2028 run: Don't wait too long after November's midterms to jump into the race. Why it matters: In the coming months, Govs. Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania, Wes Moore of Maryland, JB Pritzker of Illinois and Andy Beshear of Kentucky will face a dilemma similar to what confronted DeSantis after his 2022 reelection: Do they get in the race early — before their postelection legislative sessions start — and risk not being focused on their constituents? Or do they wait until late spring to rack up policy wins and give their opponents a head start on a White House run? Their allies and some of their teams are already debating which path to take, Democratic sources tell Axios. Driving the news: Many DeSantis aides now regret how they handled the months between DeSantis' commanding reelection victory in November 2022 and his entry into the presidential race in late May 2023, several told Axios. Donald Trump announced his reelection bid in November 2022 and began attacking DeSantis while the governor was scoring state policy wins and promoting a new book — but falling behind in the presidential race. "In this atmosphere, you can't be president by just being a great governor and boasting about your legislative wins," said Ryan Tyson, a Republican pollster and president of the Tyson Group who was a senior adviser to DeSantis. "That's how they did it in the '90s — not anymore. Enough of the voters in these early nomination contests will be driven by emotion more so than logic." A former DeSantis aide added: "There were diminishing returns for DeSantis passing conservative legislation [in Florida's 2023 session] because of his preexisting, extensive record." "I don't think it's very helpful for a Democratic governor waiting to announce for 2028 to use the legislative session to just keep doing more of what they've already been doing," the former DeSantis aide said. "It would have to be new stuff to command media attention or fix a potential political vulnerability." Reality check: The 2028 Democratic primary is different from the 2024 Republican primary. DeSantis was running against a former president who was still extraordinarily popular with the GOP base. The legal indictments against Trump led many Republican voters to rally around him. Trump also made the unorthodox move to go negative against DeSantis in paid and earned media before the Florida governor got in the race. Between the lines: If Democratic governors declare their candidacies before their legislative sessions are over, they could face attacks from rivals in the presidential race in addition to rebellions within their states. Ambitious state legislators could hold up bills and criticize newly elected governors for focusing on national politics just months after winning reelection. Axios asked Shapiro, Moore, Beshear and Pritzker if they had committed to finishing their state legislative sessions before declaring whether they were running for president. None of them directly answered the question. Shapiro spokesperson Manuel Bonder told Axios: "While we appreciate team DeSantis taking a break from banning abortion and rigging our democracy to offer unsolicited advice, I'll repeat what the governor has made clear: The midterms run through Pennsylvania, and the only thing we are focused on is winning up and down the ballot this November."

entry.title: Trump's energy boss wavers on gasoline price path
entry.body: Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Sunday cautiously predicted gasoline price relief is on the way, but stopped short of firm or precise pledges. Why it matters: Pump prices are at their highest Labor Day weekend levels on record, and the midterms loom less than two months away. His appearances on Sunday political shows also comes as diesel prices, which ripple through the economy, are at all-time highs . "I think prices headed downward is — is not an unreasonable expectation," he said on CBS's "Face the Nation." State of play: On that show and others, Wright noted that U.S. gasoline demand typically falls after Labor Day with the end of the traditional summer driving season. He also promoted recent administration moves to ease some environmental requirements for summer gasoline blends. "Gasoline production is about to go up and demand is about to go down. So, if I had to guess, they're more likely to go down than go up," Wright said on CNN's "State of the Union." Catch up quick: U.S. regular gasoline prices averaged $4.15 per gallon Sunday, per AAA data. Data: AAA; Chart: Ben Geman/Axios The intrigue: Wright also pointed to declining prices for gasoline futures contracts in the months ahead. "The marketplace thinks gasoline prices are going to move meaningfully lower. So trust the market, certainly don't trust my predictions.," he said on ABC's "This Week," per a transcript. Yes, but: Futures prices months ahead are volatile, and they're not a crystal ball for what will be happening in retail markets. Pump prices have climbed in recent weeks amid a flare-up in hostilities that has driven crude oil prices higher. Crude oil is already at its highest level in roughly six weeks, with the global benchmark above $96 per barrel at Friday's close, even though more oil appears to have been transiting the Strait of Hormuz recently. What we're watching: Oil prices could see another jump when markets open for the week, following fresh conflicts this weekend.
